title.en: Rupert Lowe urges Nigel Farage to work with Restore Britain
title.zh: 鲁珀特·洛敦促奈杰尔·法拉奇与“恢复英国”合作

summary.en: Rupert Lowe, leader of Restore Britain, has urged Nigel Farage to collaborate, stating that both should set aside personal differences and past disagreements for the good of the country.
summary.zh: “恢复英国”的领导人鲁珀特·洛呼吁奈杰尔·法拉奇与他合作，表示两人应为国家利益搁置个人恩怨和过去的意见分歧。

body.en: Lowe says pair should put ‘personalities and our past disagreements aside for good of the country’ The leader of Restore Britain has extended an olive branch to Nigel Farage, saying the two should put “personalities and our past disagreements aside for the good of the country”. Rupert Lowe told the Reform UK leader that if he was “prepared to work together around serious policies, serious reform and serious government, then so are we”. Mass deportation of illegal migrants “including women and children”. Tougher rules on legal migration, a ban on halal and kosher slaughter, the burqa, cousin marriage and sharia courts. A referendum on the death penalty. Welfare cuts to fund “self-sufficiency”. The exclusion of former Tory ministers from any future cabinet. Continue reading...
body.zh: 洛说，为了国家的利益，两人应该把“个性和我们过去的分歧放在一边”。“复兴英国”的领导人向奈杰尔·法拉奇伸出了橄榄枝，称两人应该“为了国家的利益，把个性和我们过去的分歧放在一边”。鲁珀特·洛（Rupert Lowe）告诉这位改革英国领导人，如果他“准备好围绕严肃的政策、严肃的改革和严肃的政府进行合作，那么我们也是如此”。大规模驱逐“包括妇女和儿童”的非法移民。对合法移民、清真和犹太屠宰、罩袍、表亲婚姻和伊斯兰教法庭的禁令更加严格。关于死刑的全民公投。削减福利以资助“自给自足”。将前保守党部长排除在未来内阁之外。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In the political arena, calls for unity often require individuals to set aside personal grievances and past conflicts. Colossians 3:13 reminds us of the spiritual discipline to bear with one another and forgive, just as Yahweh has forgiven us. This principle encourages leaders to prioritize the greater good over personal animosity, fostering collaboration...
reflection.zh: 在政治舞台上，呼吁团结常常要求个人放下私怨和过去的冲突。歌罗西书3:13提醒我们，要以雅伟赦免我们的方式，彼此包容，互相饶恕。这一原则鼓励领袖将大局置于个人恩怨之上，为众人的益处促进合作。

verse.textEn: Bear with each other and forgive one another if any of you has a grievance against someone.
verse.textZh: 倘若这人与那人有嫌隙，总要彼此包容，彼此饶恕。

title.en: Criticism of Reform UK’s pledge to use Navy to stop small boats – politics live
title.zh: 英国改革党动用海军阻止小型船只的承诺引来批评——政治直播

summary.en: Reform UK's proposal to use the Navy to intercept small boats carrying migrants has drawn criticism from Labour, who call it a distraction, and from a retired commander who deems it lacking substance. The issue of illegal migration has gained political prominence following a significant crossing into a Spanish enclave.
summary.zh: 英国改革党承诺动用海军阻止小型船只（载有移民）的计划受到批评。工党称此举是“转移对丑闻注意力的绝望尝试”，一位退休指挥官则认为其“缺乏实质”。自数万名摩洛哥人进入西班牙飞地以来，英国围绕非法移民的政策在政治上的重要性有所提升。

body.en: Labour say plan is a ‘desperate attempt to distract from sleaze’ while a retired commander says it ‘lacks substance’ The political saliency of the UK’s policies around illegal migration has risen since tens of thousands of people from Morocco crossed in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta last week , causing dozens of people to die (including by drowning or being crushed) and triggered a political crisis for Madrid. Spanish officials have subsequently said that almost all those who reached Ceuta on Thursday have since returned. Reform UK’s home affairs spokesperson, Zia Yusuf, said his party’s small boats plan was partly inspired by what he saw in Ceuta. He told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme this morning: I saw soldiers using pepper spray into interacting directly with migrants that were acting in a disorderly fashion. And in using the military, what I saw was Spain was able to remove, effectively send back, what looked like north of 40,000 illegal migrants in the space of a day. I truly believe there could be sufficient common ground for our two movements to cooperate collectively, destroy the looming leftwing alliance that will finish off what hope remains for this country. In my view, failing to even try because of our own personal difficulties is simply not an option. Now is the time to put our differences aside and cooperate for the good of the country that we all love. Continue reading...
body.zh: 工党称该计划是“绝望地试图分散注意力”，而一名退休指挥官则称该计划“缺乏实质内容” 自上周数万名摩洛哥人越境进入西班牙飞地休达以来，英国针对非法移民的政策的政治重要性有所上升，导致数十人死亡（包括溺水或被压死）并引发了马德里的政治危机。西班牙官员随后表示，几乎所有周四抵达休达的人都已返回。英国改革党内政事务发言人齐亚·优素福(Zia Yusuf)表示，该党的小船计划部分是受到他在休达所见所闻的启发。他今天早上告诉英国广播公司第四台“今日”节目：我看到士兵使用胡椒喷雾直接与行为不检的移民互动。通过使用军队，我看到西班牙能够在一天之内驱逐并有效遣返大约 40,000 名非法移民。我真诚地相信，我们两个运动可能有足够的共同点进行集体合作，摧毁迫在眉睫的左翼联盟，该联盟将终结这个国家仅存的希望。在我看来，因为我们个人的困难而不去尝试是不可行的。现在是抛开分歧，为了我们所热爱的国家的利益而合作的时候了。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Debates over national borders and migration often challenge societies to consider how they treat those seeking entry. Yahweh's ancient command reminds us to welcome foreigners as if they were native-born, recalling our own shared human experience of being strangers. This principle calls for compassion and equitable treatment, even amidst complex policy...
reflection.zh: 关于国家边界和移民的辩论常常挑战社会，使其思考如何对待那些寻求入境的人。雅伟古老的命令提醒我们，要像对待本地人一样欢迎外国人，并回想我们自己作为陌生人的共同人类经历。这一原则呼唤着同情心和公平待遇，即使在复杂的政策讨论中也是如此。

verse.textEn: When a foreigner resides among you in your land, do not mistreat them. The foreigner residing among you must be treated as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt.
verse.textZh: 若有外人在你们国中和你同居，就不可欺负他。和你们同居的外人，你们要看他如本地人一样，并要爱他如己，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

title.en: Middle East crisis live: Iran denies Trump’s claims that talks due to take place
title.zh: 中东危机实时报道：伊朗否认特朗普关于即将举行会谈的说法

summary.en: An Iranian spokesperson has denied claims made by the US president that talks between the two nations were scheduled to take place on Monday, stating there are no plans for a delegation exchange.
summary.zh: 伊朗发言人否认了美国总统关于两国将于周一举行会谈的说法，并表示目前没有派遣或接待代表团的计划。

body.en: Iranian spokesperson says there are no plans to receive or send a delegation following US president’s assertion that talks would take place on Monday Trump says Iran talks set for Monday Two ⁠tankers laden with ​Saudi oil crossed the Bab el-Mandeb strait over the weekend, data collected by Reuters showed on Monday, despite the maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia declared by the Iran-aligned Houthis at the end of last month. Kpler data showed that 18 commodity vessels total passed the Bab el-Mandeb strait on Sunday, down from the 27 that passed on Saturday and the 28 on Friday. Continue reading...
body.zh: 伊朗发言人表示，在美国总统声称将于周一举行会谈后，没有计划接待或派遣代表团。 特朗普表示，伊朗会谈定于周一举行。 路透社周一收集的数据显示，尽管与伊朗结盟的胡塞武装上个月末宣布对沙特阿拉伯实施海上禁运，但两艘满载沙特石油的油轮在周末穿越曼德海峡。 Kpler 数据显示，周日共有 18 艘商船通过曼德海峡，低于周六通过的 27 艘和周五的 28 艘。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In a world often marked by tension and disagreement, the pursuit of peace can feel like an uphill battle. Yahweh's word encourages us to live at peace with everyone, as far as it depends on us, even when dialogue is challenging or uncertain. This reminds us to seek understanding and reconciliation, even when paths to resolution are unclear.
reflection.zh: 在一个常常充满紧张和分歧的世界里，追求和平可能感觉像一场艰巨的战斗。雅伟的话语鼓励我们，只要我们能做到，就要与所有人和平相处，即使对话充满挑战或不确定。这提醒我们，即使解决方案的道路不明确，也要寻求理解与和解。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Central and southern Europe brace for heatwave – Europe live
title.zh: 中欧和南欧为热浪做准备——欧洲直播

summary.en: Central and southern Europe are preparing for a heatwave with temperatures expected to reach 37C in cities like Budapest and Vienna. Record low water levels in major rivers, including the Danube, are affecting the cooling capabilities of vital infrastructure, leading Hungary to switch off a nuclear plant and...
summary.zh: 中欧和南欧正准备迎接热浪，预计布达佩斯和维也纳等城市的气温将达到37摄氏度。包括多瑙河在内的主要河流水位创历史新低，影响了关键基础设施的冷却能力，导致匈牙利关闭了一座核电站，并限制了货物运输和电力生产。

body.en: Temperatures forecast to reach 37C in Budapest and Vienna as Hungary switches off vital nuclear plant with falling water levels in Danube affecting cooling capabilities Record low water levels in Europe’s major rivers have curtailed the transport of goods, reduced electricity output and shrunk company earnings, stoking fears about the economic impact of searing heat and erratic rainfall, Reuters reported. From the ⁠bustling port of Rotterdam to hydropower ​plants in Serbia , waterways have become a less reliable way to transport goods such as grains and oil, or to produce much-needed electricity when millions are seeking to cool their homes. “Given the current dynamics, it means either we’re going to see blackouts or we need to invest way more. ” Continue reading...
body.zh: 据路透社报道，匈牙利关闭了重要的核电站，多瑙河水位下降影响了冷却能力，布达佩斯和维也纳的气温预计将达到 37 摄氏度。欧洲主要河流创纪录的低水位限制了货物运输，减少了电力输出，并减少了公司收益，引发了人们对酷热和不稳定降雨对经济影响的担忧。从繁忙的鹿特丹港口到塞尔维亚的水力发电厂，当数百万人寻求为房屋降温时，水路已成为运输谷物和石油等货物或生产急需电力的不太可靠的方式。 “鉴于当前的动态，这意味着我们要么会看到停电，要么我们需要投入更多。”继续阅读...

reflection.en: The severe heatwave and critically low river levels across Europe highlight how deeply human systems are intertwined with the health of the natural world. As creation groans under environmental stress, we are reminded of our shared vulnerability and the profound impact of these changes on daily life and essential services. Yahweh's creation, though...
reflection.zh: 欧洲各地严重的酷热和河流的极低水位，凸显了人类系统与自然世界的健康状况之间密不可分的关系。当受造界在环境压力下呻吟时，我们被提醒人类共同的脆弱性，以及这些变化对日常生活和基本服务产生的深远影响。雅伟的受造界，尽管具有韧性，但也带有需要医治和谨慎管家的世界的印记。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Oil prices plunge and Europe’s stock markets rally after Trump calls off Iran strikes
title.zh: 特朗普取消对伊朗的打击后，油价暴跌，欧洲股市上涨

summary.en: Crude oil prices fell and European stock markets rose after the US president cancelled planned military strikes on Iran. The decision was made to focus on resuming negotiations for a Middle East peace deal.
summary.zh: 美国总统取消了对伊朗的军事打击计划，转而专注于恢复中东和平协议的谈判，此举导致原油价格下跌，欧洲股市上涨。

body.en: Brent crude drops by 5% after US president said talks on Middle East peace deal would resume Business live – latest updates Crude oil prices fell sharply and European stock markets rallied on Monday after Donald Trump cancelled planned strikes on Iran to focus on negotiations for a peace deal. Brent crude was trading 5% lower at $83.50 a barrel by mid-morning, after falling as low as $81.55 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate dropped more than $5 to $79.47 a barrel. Continue reading...
body.zh: 美国总统表示中东和平协议谈判将恢复，布伦特原油下跌 5% 商业直播 – 最新动态 在唐纳德·特朗普取消计划对伊朗进行的打击以专注于和平协议谈判后，周一原油价格大幅下跌，欧洲股市上涨。截至上午中旬，布伦特原油价格下跌 5%，至每桶 83.50 美元，此前曾跌至每桶 81.55 美元。美国西德克萨斯中质原油价格下跌逾 5 美元，至每桶 79.47 美元。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The decision to halt military action and pursue negotiations highlights the profound impact of choosing peace over conflict. When leaders prioritize dialogue, it can bring a tangible sense of relief and stability, reminding us of the blessing that comes with actively seeking reconciliation, for blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children...
reflection.zh: 停止军事行动并寻求谈判的决定，凸显了选择和平而非冲突的深远影响。当领导者优先考虑对话时，能带来切实的宽慰和稳定感，提醒我们积极寻求和解所带来的祝福，因为使人和平的人有福了，他们必被称为雅伟的儿女。

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
verse.textZh: 使人和睦的人有福了，因为他们必称为神的儿子。

title.en: Two workers killed in blast after re-entering quake-hit Japan mall on boss' order
title.zh: 两名员工奉老板之命重返地震受损日本商场后在爆炸中丧生

summary.en: Two women died in a blast after their employer ordered them to re-enter a quake-damaged mall to retrieve cash. The employer has since apologized for the decision.
summary.zh: 两名女性员工在老板命令她们返回受地震破坏的商场取出现金后，因爆炸身亡。该雇主已为此决定道歉。

body.en:
Two workers who died in a shopping mall explosion that followed a powerful earthquake in Japan last week were asked by a boss to re-enter the building to secure cash.

Their employer, general goods store Habita, has apologised for the "loss of two precious lives".

The two were among 38 people who died in the magnitude 6.8 earthquake in Kumamoto prefecture on 28 July. Seven of the fatalities were from Aeon Mall.

"The instructions given at the time were inappropriate, and I truly regret them," Habita sales director Goji Yuse said, NHK reported.

One of two workers has been named as 22-year-old Kurumi Otake. The identity of the other deceased employee has not been made public.

Otake's family told local media that she ran into a relative outside the Aeon Mall after the earthquake.

She told the relative that she had to go back in because her company had asked her to move money from the cash register into a safe.

This was confirmed by two company representatives, who attended Otake'a wake on Sunday and apologised to her family.

He added that the company was considering how to proceed with the matter, NHK reported.

"Looking back now, it was not worth a life," Yuse told reporters at the wake, Kyodo reported.

Otake's relative described her as someone with a "strong sense of justice". She had supported her mother after her father died three years ago, Asahi Shimbun reported.

"If she hadn't gone back inside the store at that time, Kurumi would still be with her family today," the relative said.

While most people in Aeon mall had evacuated shortly after the earthquake, some employees were still in the building about an hour later, when an explosion ripped through the mall.

Habita, founded in 1976 and operates more than ten stores across several prefectures.
body.zh: 上周日本发生强烈地震后，两名工人在购物中心爆炸中丧生，老板要求他们重新进入大楼以获取现金。 他们的雇主杂货店 Habita 已为“失去两条宝贵的生命”而道歉。 7月28日，熊本县发生6.8级地震，造成38人死亡，其中两人就是其中之一。其中七人死亡来自永旺购物中心。 据 NHK 报道，Habita 销售总监 Goji Yuse 表示：“当时给出的指示是不恰当的，我真的很遗憾。” 两名工人中的一名被命名为 22 岁的 Kurumi Otake。另一名已故员工的身份尚未公开。 大竹的家人告诉当地媒体，地震后她在永旺购物中心外遇到了一位亲戚。 她告诉亲戚，她必须回去，因为她的公司要求她把钱从收银机转移到保险箱里。 两名公司代表证实了这一点，他们参加了周日的 Otake'a 守灵活动，并向她的家人道歉。 据 NHK 报道，他补充说，该公司正在考虑如何处理此事。 据共同社报道，尤瑟在守灵仪式上对记者说：“现在回想起来，那根本不值得一条命。” 大竹的亲戚形容她是一个“具有强烈正义感”的人。据《朝日新闻》报道，三年前父亲去世后，她一直赡养母亲。 “如果当时她没有回到店里，狂三今天仍然会和家人在一起，”这位亲戚说。 虽然永旺购物中心的大多数人在地震发生后不久就撤离了，但大约一个小时后，当爆炸席卷整个购物中心时，一些员工仍在大楼内。 Habita 成立于 1976 年，在多个县经营着十多家商店。

reflection.en: This tragic incident highlights the perilous choices made when the pursuit of material wealth overshadows the value of human life. Yahweh's word reminds us that the love of money can lead to devastating consequences, as it did for these workers sent into danger. It calls us to reflect on our own priorities and ensure that the dignity and safety of people...
reflection.zh: 这起悲剧事件凸显了当对物质财富的追求盖过人生命的价值时所做出的危险选择。雅伟的话语提醒我们，贪爱钱财可能导致毁灭性的后果，就像这些被派往危险之地的工人所遭遇的那样。它呼吁我们反思自己的优先次序，确保人的尊严和安全永远优先于经济利益。

verse.textEn: For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil.
verse.textZh: 贪财是万恶之根。

title.en: As Australia is hit with mass mortalities, here’s how NZ has prepared for bird flu
title.zh: 澳大利亚遭遇大规模死亡，新西兰如何为禽流感做准备

summary.en: Australia is experiencing significant wildlife deaths due to bird flu. Its neighbor, New Zealand, has spent years researching how the lethal virus could affect its unique animal populations and preparing for such an event.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚正遭受禽流感导致的野生动物大规模死亡。其邻国新西兰已花费数年时间研究这种致命病毒将如何影响其独特的野生动物，并为此类事件做好了准备。

body.en:
When a swamp harrier hawk — known also as a kāhu — was found tangled in a fence in a thinly populated part of New Zealand's North Island in early July, no one thought much about the discovery.

But when the battered scavenger was put down the following day after its health deteriorated, a routine test would enshrine the bird in history.

It was the first native New Zealand bird to test positive for the highly virulent, often lethal strain of H5N1 bird flu which had been detected on Australia's mainland for the first time just a month prior.

"There's lots of birds that go between Australia and New Zealand; although there is a sea between us, we're way more connected than we might like to think," says Jemma Geoghegan from the University of Otago.

A month on, the virus is slowly making its way into the region's eco-systems. New Zealand has recorded two cases of the virus but officials there expect that number to start climbing steeply any day now.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Australia, meanwhile, has just recorded its first mass casualty event: 49 dead greater crested terns and 35 sick ones were discovered on rocks off Cape Jaffa, an isolated outcrop on South Australia's rugged limestone coast.

Both countries knew the virus was not far off when it was first detected on Australia's remote sub-Antarctic Heard Island in 2025, leading to mass mortality of elephant seals.

By this time, preparations for the strain — which has ripped through every other continent — were well underway in New Zealand, where for the past two years the country's Department of Conservation has been trialling a vaccination program for six species of "highly" endangered birds.

Two years ago the country began researching how certain native birds would tolerate and respond to the vaccine, so when the disease made its inevitable landfall, these populations could be protected.

"The trial was really to understand if the vaccine was going to be effective, but also what kind of doses different birds might need."

She said this "targeted program" had been rolled out for species that were "really, really endangered" and already "highly managed" through GPS trackers and health monitoring.

The vaccine being used in New Zealand requires a booster shot to be effective, so it's important that researchers are able to carefully track which birds have had the jab and which haven't.

"Often they'll be on offshore islands that are highly managed, because there's only maybe a few 100 left of the individuals."

reflection.en: The foresight shown by New Zealand in preparing for a potential bird flu outbreak among its unique wildlife reminds us of the wisdom in foreseeing danger. Yahweh's wisdom encourages us to be prudent stewards, taking proactive steps to protect vulnerable creation from harm. Such preparation reflects a responsible approach to the challenges facing our world.

title.en: Ariana Grande to take a break from public life amid 'endless' scrutiny
title.zh: 爱莉安娜·格兰德因“无休止的审视”将暂停公众生活

summary.en: US singer Ariana Grande, 33, plans to step back from public visibility after her world tour next month, citing "endless scrutiny" as the reason for her break.
summary.zh: 美国歌手爱莉安娜·格兰德（33岁）的代表表示，她将在下个月世界巡演结束后“退出公众视线”，原因是“无休止的审视”。

body.en:
Ariana Grande is to withdraw from public appearances and will no longer star in an upcoming musical production in London when she ends her Eternal Sunshine tour next month.

A representative for the US singer, 33, told People magazine that she "will be taking a step back from visibility" when the tour ends, after her appearances led to "endless, ongoing public scrutiny".

The company behind a revival of Stephen Sondheim's Sunday in the Park with George, due to play at the Barbican in 2027, confirmed that she would no longer be part of the production and had its "complete understanding and support".

Grande's physical appearance and health have been a topic of speculation in recent years.

This speculation has increased since the release of her latest album, Petal, which was released on Friday, and her appearance in promotional material for the launch.

In the music video, Grande plays a performer who is repeatedly told in auditions that she is "not good enough", is "desperate" and that she "should get some work done" then that she has "too much work done." The character eventually takes a chainsaw to the critics.

Grande's representative stressed to People that the star was looking forward to finishing her tour "on a high note, both healthily and happily, and then taking a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances, which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny".

They added: "She performs a very physical show, and there is a lot of athleticism involved. She performs healthily and successfully at a very high level night after night."

Fans expressed a combination of support for the star and concern about her wellbeing, with the message #weloveyouariana trending on social media.

Her tour continues in Chicago on Monday, with three dates at the city's United Center. It will then move to London's O2 arena for 10 dates from 15 August, with the tour concluding there on 1 September.

The Thank U, Next and 7 Rings singer was billed to appear alongside her Wicked co-star, British actor Jonathan Bailey, in the new production of Sondheim's critically acclaimed 1984 musical.

A representative for Empire Street Productions confirmed to the BBC that the musical would go ahead without Grande.

"Following this evening's announcement from Ariana Grande's team, we can confirm that she has decided to step back from Sunday in the Park with George," they said.

"We know this cannot have been an easy decision, and she makes it with our complete understanding and support. We wish her nothing but the best."

A replacement for Grande in the West End revival of the Pulitzer Prize–winning musical has not yet been named.

body.zh: 爱莉安娜·格兰德下个月结束“永恒阳光”巡演后，将不再公开露面，也不会再出演伦敦即将上映的音乐作品。 这位 33 岁的美国歌手的一位代表告诉《人物》杂志，巡演结束后，她“将退出知名度”，因为她的露面引发了“无休止、持续的公众监督”。 斯蒂芬·桑德海姆 (Stephen Sondheim) 的《周日公园与乔治》(Sunday in the Park with George) 将于 2027 年在巴比肯艺术中心 (Barbican) 重演，该公司确认她将不再参与制作，并得到了“完全理解和支持”。 近年来，格兰德的外貌和健康状况一直是人们猜测的话题。 自从她周五发行的最新专辑《Petal》以及她出现在该专辑的宣传材料中以来，这种猜测有所增加。 在音乐视频中，格兰德饰演一名表演者，她在试镜时多次被告知她“不够好”，“绝望”，她“应该完成一些工作”，然后她“完成了太多的工作”。这个角色最终用电锯对待批评者。 格兰德的代表向《人物》杂志强调，这位明星期待着“健康快乐地高调结束她的巡演，然后从面向公众的工作和露面中休息一下，这导致了无休止的、持续的公众监督”。 他们补充道：“她的表演非常具有身体素质，并且涉及很多运动能力。她每晚都以非常高的水平健康且成功地表演。” 粉丝们表达了对这位明星的支持和对她健康的担忧，#weloveyouariana 的信息在社交媒体上流行。 她的巡演将于周一在芝加哥继续，在该市的联合中心举行三场演出。随后，演出将移师伦敦 O2 体育馆，从 8 月 15 日起举行 10 场演出，巡演将于 9 月 1 日结束。 这位演唱《Thank U》、《Next》和《7 Rings》的歌手预计将与她在《魔法坏女巫》中的搭档、英国演员乔纳森·贝利 (Jonathan Bailey) 一起出演桑德海姆广受好评的 1984 年音乐剧的新作品。 帝国街制作公司的一位代表向 BBC 证实，这部音乐剧将在没有格兰德的情况下继续进行。 他们说：“在今晚爱莉安娜·格兰德团队宣布之后，我们可以确认她已决定从周日与乔治一起退出公园。” “我们知道这不是一个容易的决定，她在我们的完全理解和支持下做出了这个决定。我们祝她一切顺利。” 这部普利策奖获奖音乐剧在西区重演的格兰德的替代者尚未确定。 获取我们的旗舰新闻通讯，其中包含您开始新的一天所需的所有头条新闻。在这里注册。

reflection.en: The constant "endless scrutiny" of public life can be a profound test, much like a crucible refines precious metals. This decision to step back highlights the immense pressure that comes with fame, reminding us that character is often forged and revealed under the intense gaze of others. Yahweh sees the heart, beyond the fleeting judgments of the crowd.
reflection.zh: 持续不断的公众“无休止的审视”可能是一种深刻的考验，就像坩埚提炼贵金属一样。这一退出公众视线的决定，突显了名声所带来的巨大压力，提醒我们品格往往是在他人密切关注下被塑造和显明的。雅伟洞察人心，超越了人群转瞬即逝的评判。

verse.textEn: The crucible for silver and the furnace for gold, but people are tested by their praise.
verse.textZh: 鼎为炼银，炉为炼金，人的称赞也试炼人。

title.en: Trump suggests new talks with Iran to begin on Monday
title.zh: 特朗普建议周一与伊朗重启谈判

summary.en: President Trump has proposed new talks with Iran to begin on Monday, though Tehran has not yet responded to the suggestion. This comes after previous claims by Trump that a negotiated end to the conflict was near, only for military strikes to resume.
summary.zh: 特朗普总统提议周一与伊朗重启谈判，但德黑兰尚未对此建议作出回应。此前，特朗普曾表示冲突的谈判解决已近在咫尺，但随后军事打击又重新开始。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has said new talks with Iran will begin on Monday, after calling off what he said would have been "massive" strikes on the country.

"They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming," he told reporters on board Air Force One on Sunday. "We're talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon."

In an earlier post on Truth Social, Trump said he had been asked by Iran and US allies in the Middle East to "hold off" on any attack as the "perimeters" of a deal had been agreed.

Iran's foreign ministry said there are no plans to receive a US delegation or send Iranians to Washington. Earlier talks have been facilitated through mediators.

The US president has repeatedly vowed that a negotiated end to the war is near, only for tit-for-tat strikes to resume.

In his remarks on Air Force One, Trump declined to outline a deadline for a deal to be struck with Tehran, adding: "We'll just see how it is. We're ready to go anytime we want... I'm not looking to kill people."

Trump added that Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman - as well as US partners such as the United Arab Emirates and Qatar - had urged him against conducting strikes over the weekend.

"We were all set to go," Trump said. "The reason they asked is [that] they think there's a deal," he said. "There's a deal on Hormuz, and there will be a deal on the nuclear."

Global oil prices fell on Monday morning in Asia trading after Trump's announcement. Brent Crude oil was down by 4.5% at $83.98 (£62.26), while US-traded oil was 4.6% lower at $80.74 (£59.85).

Energy prices have fluctuated since the conflict started on 28 February as traders reacted to disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Around 20% of the world's crude oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) usually flows through the strait.

Iran's semi-official Mehr news agency denied that Tehran had asked the US to hold off on further military action, saying Trump's claims were "nothing but a new lie".

On Sunday, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that negotiations with Oman on a deal on the Strait of Hormuz were "on track for finalisation", according to Iranian media.

The US president has not yet made clear the venue for the talks on Monday, nor the potential attendees.

During his remarks on Air Force One, Trump said that the planned strikes would have been "the biggest attack since World War II", and could have derailed prospects of a negotiated end to the months-long war.

Trump declined to answer if he had been planning to strike Iranian energy infrastructure, which international law experts have said could constitute a war crime .

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.

title.en: US and Japan take action to prop up yen in rare joint move
title.zh: 美日罕见联合行动以支撑日元

summary.en: The United States and Japan have announced a rare joint intervention to stabilize the yen, indicating their readiness to take further coordinated action if needed.
summary.zh: 美国和日本宣布采取罕见的联合行动以稳定日元汇率，并表示未来将毫不犹豫地进行联合干预。

body.en:
Japan and the US have confirmed that they jointly intervened last week to halt a slide in the yen after it fell to a fresh 40-year low.

The joint intervention is the first since 2011, when both countries took coordinated action to weaken the yen after the devastating earthquake and tsunami that hit eastern Japan.

Both Japan's Ministry of Finance and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have said that they will not hesitate to conduct more joint interventions in the future.

It highlights both countries' efforts to prevent a sell-off in the yen and Japanese government bonds from having an impact on the global economy, including potentially helping to push up borrowing costs for Washington.

Bank of Japan data indicated that Tokyo may have sold almost $59bn of US dollars to buy yen when it intervened in New York markets on Thursday, before Friday's confirmed joint intervention with Washington.

The US has not confirmed the size of its intervention, but a Reuters photograph of a notepad in front of Bessent during a cabinet meeting on Friday read: "To Do: Buy Japanese Yen $5-10 bil".

Shigeto Nagai, head of Japan economics at Oxford Economics, told the BBC: "The United States agreed to participate in the coordinated intervention because it serves its national interests by offering the prospect of significant benefits at a low cost."

The two countries are expected to continue to intervene "intermittently in a coordinated manner for some time", he added.

"Even if the actual amount of intervention is not particularly large, the prolonged sense of vigilance regarding intervention will be effective in deterring speculators."

The yen is historically weak mainly due to Japan having much lower central bank interest rates than other major economies like the US. That makes the Japanese currency less attractive to international investors.

The Bank of Japan last raised interest rates in June, as it increased its main rate to 1% - the highest level since September 1995. In comparison, the US Federal Reserve's benchmark rate is in a range of 3.50% to 3.75%.

Japan also faces other issues including a decades-long slide in its working-age population, low productivity and a heavy reliance on energy imports that are priced in US dollars.

On Monday, Japan's finance ministry said Friday's intervention with the US Treasury Department "countered excessive volatility and disorderly movements in the Japanese yen in recent months".

The "coordinated foreign exchange actions countered disorderly yen movements," Bessent said in a social media post.

"We strongly support Japan's decisive market and monetary steps to correct the substantial undervaluation of the yen," he added.

"They have a weakening yen, and they wanted a little bit of help. And we're always there for...
body.zh: 日本和美国已确认上周联合干预，以阻止日元跌至 40 年来的新低后的下滑。 此次联合干预是自2011年以来的首次，当时两国在日本东部发生毁灭性地震和海啸后采取协调行动压低日元汇率。 日本财务省和美国财长斯科特·贝森特均表示，未来将毫不犹豫地进行更多联合干预。 它凸显了两国为防止日元和日本政府债券抛售对全球经济产生影响而做出的努力，包括可能有助于推高华盛顿的借贷成本。 牛津经济研究院日本经济学负责人永井茂人告诉英国广播公司：“美国同意参与协调干预，因为它可以以低成本提供显着利益的前景，从而符合其国家利益。” 他补充说，预计两国将继续“在一段时间内以协调的方式间歇性地进行干预”。 “即使实际的干预量不是特别大，但对干预的长期警惕感也会有效震慑投机者。” 日元历史上疲软的主要原因是日本央行利率远低于美国等其他主要经济体。这使得日元对国际投资者的吸引力下降。 日本央行上次加息是在6月，将主要利率提高至1%，为1995年9月以来的最高水平。相比之下，美联储的基准利率在3.50%至3.75%之间。 日本还面临其他问题，包括劳动年龄人口长达数十年的下滑、生产率低下以及严重依赖以美元计价的能源进口。 日本财务省周一表示，周五对美国财政部的干预“遏制了日元近几个月来的过度波动和无序波动”。 贝森特在社交媒体上发帖称，“协调一致的外汇行动对抗了日元的无序波动”。 他补充说：“我们强烈支持日本采取果断的市场和货币措施，以纠正日元大幅低估的情况。” “他们的日元走弱，他们需要一点帮助。我们始终支持日本，”美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周日告诉记者。 特朗普发表言论后，美元兑日元下跌0.2%，至157.07日元，远低于上个月164的40年高点，但在日本财务省发表声明后，美元兑日元回升至157.70日元。 日本央行数据显示，东京周四干预纽约市场时，可能已抛售近 590 亿美元购买日元。

reflection.en: In complex global economics, the decision by the US and Japan to act together highlights the importance of seeking broad counsel. When nations collaborate on major policy decisions, it underscores the wisdom found in collective guidance for the well-being of their people and the global economy.
reflection.zh: 在复杂的全球经济中，美国和日本决定共同行动，凸显了寻求广泛建议的重要性。当国家就重大政策决策进行合作时，这强调了为两国人民和全球经济福祉而寻求集体指导的智慧。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: Aung San Suu Kyi appears healthy in first confirmed outside contact for 2.5 years
title.zh: 昂山素季在两年半以来首次确认的外部接触中显得健康

summary.en: Myanmar's military government has released new photos showing detained leader Aung San Suu Kyi meeting with an official from the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). This marks the first confirmed outside contact for Suu Kyi in two and a half years, and she reportedly appeared healthy.
summary.zh: 缅甸军政府发布了新照片，显示被拘禁的领导人昂山素季与红十字国际委员会（ICRC）的一名官员会面。这是昂山素季两年半以来首次获得确认的外部接触，据报道她看起来身体健康。

body.en:
Detained Burmese leader Aung San Suu Kyi has been allowed to meet a delegation from the International Federation of the Red Cross, the first confirmed outside contact with her since a letter to her son two and a half years ago.

In photographs of the meeting released by the military government Suu Kyi appeared to be healthy.

She was detained shortly after the armed forces deposed her government in 2021, and sentenced to 33 years in jail on what are widely viewed as trumped-up charges, though her sentence has been reduced and she has been moved to house arrest .

Despite repeated assurances from the military that Suu Kyi is alive and well, they have never provided any convincing evidence of this.

Her son Kim Aris has in recent months mounted an international campaign demanding proof of life for the 81-year-old democracy icon.

Now a delegation from the ICRC has been allowed to meet her – her first confirmed meeting with anyone outside the government for nearly four years.

Photographs released of her with the ICRC team show Suu Kyi looking relaxed and well, although no details of her state of health have been given, nor of what they talked about.

The Myanmar government, still headed by coup leader Min Aung Hlaing and dominated by the military despite an election held earlier this year, is trying to end its diplomatic isolation in a series of official visits to neighbouring countries.

Among the top demands being made of Myanmar's military leadership is that they end the aerial bombardment of opposition-held areas, start negotiations to end the civil war, and release Aung San Suu Kyi.

They have so far rejected those calls, but the publication of this morning's meeting suggests they may be willing to accede to the last demand.
body.zh: 被拘留的缅甸领导人昂山素季获准会见红十字国际联合会代表团，这是自两年半前给她儿子的一封信以来首次确认与她有外部接触。 在军政府公布的会议照片中，昂山素季似乎很健康。 2021 年武装部队推翻政府后不久，她就被拘留，并因被广泛认为捏造的指控而被判处 33 年监禁，不过她的刑期已被减刑，并已被软禁。 尽管军方一再保证昂山素季还活着并且身体健康，但他们从未提供任何令人信服的证据。 她的儿子金·阿里斯 (Kim Aris) 近几个月发起了一场国际运动，要求提供这位 81 岁民主偶像的生命证明。 现在，红十字国际委员会的一个代表已获准会见她，这是近四年来她首次确认与政府以外的任何人会面。 公布的昂山素季与红十字国际委员会工作组在一起的照片显示，昂山素季看起来很轻松、健康，但没有透露她的健康状况以及他们谈论的内容。 尽管今年早些时候举行了选举，缅甸政府仍由政变领导人敏昂莱领导，并由军方主导，并试图通过对邻国的一系列正式访问来结束其外交孤立。 缅甸军方领导层提出的首要要求之一是停止对反对派控制地区的空中轰炸，开始结束内战的谈判，并释放昂山素季。 到目前为止，他们拒绝了这些呼吁，但今天上午会议的公布表明他们可能愿意接受最后一个要求。

reflection.en: The long isolation of a national leader by a military government highlights the vulnerability of a people under authoritarian rule. Proverbs 28:15 reminds us that a wicked ruler can be like a dangerous predator over a helpless populace, underscoring the profound impact of leadership on a nation's well-being. In such times, the longing for justice and...
reflection.zh: 一位国家领导人被军政府长期隔离，凸显了人民在威权统治下的脆弱性。箴言28:15提醒我们，邪恶的统治者对无助的人民来说，就像危险的捕食者，这强调了领导力对国家福祉的深远影响。在这样的时期，对公义和自由的渴望往往会变得更加强烈，并由对雅伟最终干预的盼望所支撑。

verse.textEn: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
verse.textZh: 暴虐的君王辖制贫民，好像吼叫的狮子、觅食的熊。

title.en: Cuba suffers yet another nationwide blackout
title.zh: 古巴再次遭遇全国性停电

summary.en: Cuba has experienced another nationwide power outage, the fourth since July, as its electricity grid continues to struggle under a US-imposed oil blockade.
summary.zh: 古巴再次遭遇全国性停电，这是继七月以来第四次，该国电网在美国实施的石油禁运下持续面临困境。

body.en:
Cuba's electricity grid has collapsed again after three nationwide blackouts in July. The power failure comes amid a US-imposed oil blockade on the communist island.

  Cuba 's state-owned grid operator said the island's power system collapsed late on Sunday, the latest in a series of rolling power cuts caused by aging infrastructure and a US energy embargo .

The state-run utility UNE said there was a "total disconnection" of the national electricity system, which means the entire country of 10 million people, including the capital, Havana, has been plunged into darkness.

The Ministry of Energy said that protocols to reactivate the grid were underway.

The series of outages afflicting the island in recent times have also affected water supplies and cooling systems, making normal life extremely difficult.

Cuba, which relies largely on aging oil-fired power plants, lost access to fuel from its previous primary supplier, Venezuela, after US President Donald Trump imposed an oil blockade following Washington's ouster and capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro on January 3 .  

Imports from Mexico , which subsequently became Cuba's key supplier of oil, have also ceased under US pressure.

Supplies brought by a single Russian tanker in March with Washington's authorization have been exhausted.

Cuba is also facing other pressure from the US, including ramped-up sanctions against Cuban state-owned businesses imposed by the Trump administration.

These have led to a number of foreign companies suspending their operations in the island.

Washington has also indicted former President Raul Castro over the downing of two civilian planes 30 years ago, in which three US citizens and a US resident died. 

The US redesignated the communist island as a "state sponsor of terrorism" for a third time in 2025, shortly after former President Joe Biden moved to have it deleted from the list.

body.zh: 7月份全国三次停电后，古巴电网再次崩溃。停电发生在美国对这个共产主义岛屿实施石油封锁之际。 古巴国有电网运营商表示，该岛的电力系统于周日晚间崩溃，这是由于基础设施老化和美国能源禁运导致的一系列轮流停电中的最新一起。 国营公用事业公司UNE表示，国家电力系统“完全断电”，这意味着包括首都哈瓦那在内的整个1000万人口的国家陷入了黑暗。 能源部表示，重新启动电网的协议正在进行中。 最近困扰该岛的一系列停电也影响了供水和冷却系统，使正常生活变得极其困难。 古巴主要依赖老化的燃油发电厂，1 月 3 日美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在华盛顿推翻并俘虏委内瑞拉总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗后实施石油封锁，导致古巴失去了从其以前的主要供应商委内瑞拉获得燃料的机会。 在美国的压力下，墨西哥也停止了进口，墨西哥随后成为古巴的主要石油供应国。 一艘俄罗斯油轮在华盛顿授权下于三月份运送的物资已经耗尽。 古巴还面临来自美国的其他压力，包括特朗普政府加大对古巴国有企业的制裁力度。 这些导致许多外国公司暂停在岛上的业务。 华盛顿还就30年前击落两架民用飞机、造成三名美国公民和一名美国居民死亡的事件起诉前总统劳尔·卡斯特罗。 在前总统乔·拜登将这个共产主义岛屿从名单中删除后不久，美国于 2025 年第三次将这个共产主义岛屿重新指定为“支持恐怖主义的国家”。 不要让算法隐藏新闻。如果您信赖我们团队的可信报道，请花点时间点击此处并点击“星标”或“首选”按钮，选择我们作为您在 Google 上的首选来源，这样您始终会首先看到我们经过验证的新闻。

reflection.en: For those enduring repeated power outages and economic hardship, the daily struggle can feel overwhelming. Yet, even in prolonged crises, we can find solace in the enduring faithfulness of Yahweh, whose mercies are renewed each morning, offering strength for another day.

title.en: 'Deeply saddened': Australian helicopter provider speaks after Greece firefighting tragedy
title.zh: “深感悲痛”：希腊消防悲剧后，澳大利亚直升机供应商发声

summary.en: McDermott Aviation, an Australian helicopter provider, has expressed profound sadness following a firefighting tragedy in Greece, where helicopters leased by the company were involved as wildfires continue to spread across southern Europe.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚直升机供应商麦克德莫特航空对希腊消防悲剧表示深切哀悼，该公司租赁的直升机参与了扑灭南欧持续蔓延的野火。

body.en:
Two crew members have died after two helicopters — leased by Australian company McDermott Aviation — collided midair while battling wildfires in Greece on Sunday.

A Greek and a Danish national were killed in the crash over Psatha, an area west of Athens, according to Greece's fire service. Two crew members from Greece and Britain who were operating a separate helicopter were found alive.

Founder and president of McDermott Aviation, John McDermott said he was "deeply saddened" by news of the fatal collision.

"We are deeply saddened to confirm that the two crew members aboard one of the helicopters have lost their lives. The two crew members from the second helicopter are in the care of medical professionals.

"Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with the families, friends and colleagues of those affected by this tragic incident. Both crews were undertaking the critical work of supporting firefighting operations to help protect communities."

McDermott Aviation has reportedly operated in Greece for several years. The company said it is working closely with relevant authorities as they undertake an investigation into the cause of the incident.

Over the past decade, McDermott Aviation said it has engaged in around 10 to 12 international movements a year via sea and air freight. It also operates in New Caledonia, Papua New Guinea, Indonesia and the United States, which is currently experiencing wildfires in several western states.

Nikos Pagiotelis has been a volunteer firefighter in Greece for more than 20 years. He told SBS Greek about the moment he heard news of the crash over local radio.

"When you are inside the fire, and you are trying to help the people, you're trying to save the animals, save the forest. Then suddenly [you] hear that two helicopters have crashed a couple of miles near you — you can understand that something really hurts inside," Pagiotelis said.

"You can do nothing, you freeze for a little bit, and then you just continue your work. You continue to help people to honour the lives of the loss of two comrades."

In a statement on social media, Greek prime minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis also expressed his "sorrow for the tragic accident" and extended condolences to the families of the deceased firefighters.

"The loss of the Greek coordinator and the Danish pilot at the time they were attempting the major fire in Porto Gremeno fills us all with grief," Mitsotakis said.

Nearly 500 firefighters and 23 aircraft have been deployed to fight fires in Greece, which have been driven by high temperatures and gale-force winds.

In moments of such grief, we hold onto the promise that Yahweh will one day wipe away every tear, and death, mourning, crying, and pain will be no more. title.en: Man arrested over death of British woman found in suitcase in Athens
title.zh: 男子因雅典行李箱女尸案被捕

summary.en: A man has been arrested in connection with the death of Elisabeth-Jane Ross, a Scottish national whose body was found last month in a suitcase in a derelict building in Athens.
summary.zh: 一名男子因涉嫌苏格兰公民伊丽莎白-简·罗斯的死亡而被捕。她的尸体上个月在雅典一栋废弃建筑的行李箱中被发现。

body.en:
The body of Scottish national Elisabeth-Jane Ross was discovered last month in a suitcase in a derelict building in Athens.

A 26-year-old man has been arrested by Greek police in connection with the death of a British woman whose body was found in a suitcase in Athens last month.

"Officers of the Directorate for Combating Organized Crime have solved the homicide of a 38-year-old UK national, whose body was found inside a suitcase in an abandoned building in the Kypseli area on July 18," the Hellenic Police said on Sunday.

The victim, identified in British and Greek media reports as 38-year-old Elisabeth-Jane Ross from Scotland, arrived in Greece in late June and was last known to be in the Athens area on July 10. She was later reported missing.

Police said the suspect, a foreign national, confessed on Thursday and now faces charges including intentional homicide, robbery and firearms-related offenses.

"It emerged that the [suspect] placed the body in a suitcase and transported it to the abandoned premises. Furthermore, in the days that followed, the 26-year-old used the victim's bank cards to withdraw sums of money," police said.

According to reports, the suspect said the victim was already dead when he found her, although police made no mention of this in their statement.

Greek police said international cooperation, including support from Interpol authorities in the US and UK law enforcement agencies, helped identify the victim despite advanced decomposition.

body.zh: 上个月，苏格兰国民伊丽莎白·简·罗斯的尸体在雅典一座废弃建筑的手提箱中被发现。 一名 26 岁男子因与上个月在雅典的一个手提箱中发现的一名英国妇女的死亡有关而被希腊警方逮捕。 希腊警方周日表示：“打击有组织犯罪局的官员已经侦破了一名 38 岁英国国民的凶杀案，7 月 18 日，他的尸体在基普塞利地区一栋废弃建筑的手提箱内被发现。” 英国和希腊媒体报道称，受害者是来自苏格兰的 38 岁伊丽莎白·简·罗斯 (Elisabeth-Jane Ross)，她于 6 月下旬抵达希腊，最后一次获知是在 7 月 10 日在雅典地区。后来据报道她失踪了。 警方表示，嫌疑人是一名外国人，他于周四认罪，目前面临包括故意杀人、抢劫和枪支相关犯罪在内的指控。 警方称，“嫌疑人将尸体放入手提箱，运至废弃场所。此外，在接下来的几天里，这名26岁的男子使用受害者的银行卡提取了一笔钱。” 据报道，嫌疑人称，当他发现受害人时，她已经死亡，但警方在声明中没有提及这一点。 希腊警方表示，国际合作，包括美国国际刑警组织和英国执法机构的支持，帮助确认了受害者的身份，尽管受害者已被严重分解。 不要让算法隐藏新闻。如果您信赖我们团队的可信报道，请花点时间选择我们作为您在 Google 上的首选来源，这样您始终会首先看到我们经过验证的新闻。

reflection.en: This tragic news reminds us of the profound value of every human life, created in the image of Yahweh. When a life is violently taken, it is a grievous offense against that inherent dignity. We pray for justice for Elisabeth-Jane Ross and for comfort for all who mourn her.
reflection.zh: 这则悲剧性的新闻提醒我们，每个人的生命都具有深远的价值，因为我们是雅伟照着自己的形象创造的。当一个生命被暴力夺走时，这是对这种内在尊严的严重冒犯。我们为伊丽莎白-简·罗斯祈求公义，也为所有哀悼她的人祈求安慰。

title.en: Israel kills 18 in Gaza despite Trump's announcement of Hamas disarmament deal
title.zh: 以色列袭击加沙致18人死亡，部长称无协议停止攻击

summary.en: Israeli airstrikes in Gaza have resulted in 18 deaths, continuing despite a US announcement of a potential path for Hamas' disarmament. A minister stated there is no agreement to halt the attacks.
summary.zh: 尽管美国宣布了哈马斯解除武装的途径，以色列对加沙的空袭仍在继续，造成18人死亡。一位部长表示，目前没有停止袭击的协议。

body.en:
Israeli airstrikes hit Gaza for a second straight day on Monday, killing at least 18 Palestinians, medics said, despite US President Donald Trump's announcement of a breakthrough in efforts to implement last year's ceasefire agreement.

From dawn, Israeli warplanes hit Gaza City in the north, the central city of Deir al-Balah and the southern area of Khan Younis, causing the biggest daily death toll in weeks, according to Palestinian health officials.

Trump's assertion on Friday that Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups had agreed to disarm had raised hopes of a turning point in efforts to end the conflict.

On Sunday, Israeli energy minister Eli Cohen — a member of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's security cabinet — said the government would give Hamas the opportunity to disarm but that he was "very sceptical" that would happen.

Cohen told Israel's Army Radio there had been no deal to halt attacks on Gaza and that he saw a need for Israel, which already occupies 70 per cent of the enclave, to take full control of it if Hamas did not disarm.

title.en: Trump says fresh Iran talks set to begin after major strikes called off
title.zh: 特朗普称取消重大打击后，新的伊朗谈判即将开始

summary.en: Former President Trump announced that new talks with Iran are expected to commence after planned military strikes were called off. Mediators are working to restore a June memorandum of understanding, though the path to a lasting peace agreement remains challenging.
summary.zh: 前总统特朗普宣布，在取消了原定的军事打击后，与伊朗的新一轮谈判即将开始。尽管和平之路依然充满挑战，伊朗调解员仍在努力恢复六月份的谅解备忘录。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump says new negotiations with Iran will begin on Monday, after he decided to hold off on striking the Islamic republic to pursue a deal to end the war that's now entering its sixth month.

Trump told reporters on Monday that the talks would cover the Strait of Hormuz — a route for global energy supplies that has become a key sticking point in the conflict — and ultimately, the de-nuclearisation of Iran.

For its part, Iran said it was nearing a deal with Oman over a new route through the strait, where a tanker reported an explosion nearby on Monday, underscoring the continued volatility of the strategic waterway.

The US and Iran have been at war since 28 February, when the US and Israel launched surprise strikes against Iran, though months of on-off diplomacy have led to periods of relative calm.

Following a return to strikes last month, fears had mounted that the fighting could escalate once again. Trump had threatened to hit Iran "very hard" and was reportedly considering renewed attacks, including against energy infrastructure, with US embassies across the region on alert.

Trump pulled back from that threat Saturday, saying the "perimeters" of a deal were there.

"Now what we're doing is we're talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon," Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One on Sunday, without providing details of the venue or participants in the talks.

The US president said he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on the strikes, which he claimed would have been "the biggest attack since World War II".

A previous ceasefire deal that included the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz fell through, and Iran has since tightened its control over the waterway.

The US president said at the start of the conflict that the war was necessary to deal with Iran's nuclear program. Western nations accuse Iran of seeking a bomb, though Iran insists the program is entirely civilian in nature.

Iranian politician Hassan Ghashghavi, spokesman for the parliament's national security commission, said on Sunday that mediators were trying to revive the so-called Islamabad memorandum of understanding, which was agreed in June.

That memorandum was not intended as a final peace deal, but as a stepping stone to negotiations on a comprehensive agreement, though it did include provisions on Hormuz.

"They know that the main issue and, in fact, the key to the matter right now is the issue of the Strait of Hormuz, so yes, there is an exchange of views," Ghashghavi said.

title.en: Small insects, big damage: The global ant trade is booming
title.zh: 小昆虫，大破坏：全球蚂蚁贸易正在蓬勃发展

summary.en: The global trade in African ants, both legal and illegal, is experiencing a boom, with these insects being shipped to Europe. This growing trade raises concerns about its appeal to hobbyists and the potential risks it poses to various ecosystems, including the possibility of causing power outages.
summary.zh: 非洲蚂蚁的全球贸易（无论合法与否）正在蓬勃发展，这些昆虫被运往欧洲。这种日益增长的贸易引发了人们对其对爱好者的吸引力以及对包括停电在内的各种生态系统可能造成的风险的担忧。

body.en:
Legal or not, the trade in African ants bound for Europe is booming. What do hobbyists find appealing about these insects, and what risks does the trade pose to ecosystems, including power outages?

They are unusual pieces of evidence that regularly appear in Kenyan  courtrooms: thousands of ants packed into tiny containers.

Since 2025, such finds have been presented in court several times. Staff from the Kenya Wildlife Service discovered them during baggage inspections. In multiple cases, they identified thousands of specimens of the sought-after Messor Cephalotes species also known as the Giant African Harvester Ant . A single queen can fetch more than €200 ($230) on the market.

The export of wild animals is generally prohibited in Kenya. Due to high levels of poaching — particularly involving elephants and rhinoceroses — many African countries have introduced tough laws against wildlife trafficking.

Kenya has also tightened its legislation. Under these rules, a Chinese  national who attempted to export ants was sentenced last April to one year in prison for biopiracy. Given the growing scale of smuggling and its ecological consequences , the judge said the sentence should serve as a deterrent.

It was already the second major ant-smuggling case in 12 months. The previous year, the wildlife service stopped four men who referred to themselves as the "Ant Gang." Among them were two 19-year-old Belgians  who were trying to smuggle 5,500 queens to Europe. They were fined around €5,000 each.

Whenever such cases arise, authorities often call entomologist Dino Martins to the airport. "I was shocked," he said. "Not only by the sheer number of ants, but also because they were queen ants."

The seized insects were young queens that had been dug up from nests in the ground, according to Martins, who has led several research institutes in Kenya and is regarded as one of Africa's leading ant experts, These queens have wings that allow them to fly away and establish new colonies.

"When you collect queens at this critical moment, you interrupt a key stage in the creation of new colonies," he said, adding that Kenya's ecosystems are also affected because ants transport grass seeds, helping to regenerate the savannah.

In Europe, keeping ants as pets has become increasingly popular, particularly among young people. Colonies are housed in glass terrariums where a queen produces offspring and establishes an entirely new population.

One person who keeps ants as a hobby is Michael Meier, who asked not to be identified by his real name. While at university, he wanted a pet that required little attention.

"With ants, it doesn't really matter whether I feed them today or tomorrow," he said.

body.zh: 无论合法与否，运往欧洲的非洲蚂蚁贸易正在蓬勃发展。爱好者们对这些昆虫有何吸引力？这种贸易对生态系统造成了哪些风险，包括停电？ 它们是肯尼亚法庭上经常出现的不寻常证据：数千只蚂蚁被装在小容器里。 自 2025 年以来，此类调查结果已多次提交法庭。肯尼亚野生动物管理局的工作人员在行李检查时发现了它们。在多个案例中，他们鉴定了数千个备受追捧的 Messor Cephalotes 物种（也称为巨型非洲收割蚁）的标本。单个蜂王在市场上的售价可以超过 200 欧元（230 美元）。 肯尼亚普遍禁止出口野生动物。由于偷猎现象严重（特别是涉及大象和犀牛），许多非洲国家都出台了严厉的法律来打击野生动物贩运。 肯尼亚还加强了立法。根据这些规定，去年四月，一名试图出口蚂蚁的中国公民因生物剽窃被判处一年监禁。鉴于走私规模不断扩大及其对生态造成的影响，法官表示，该判决应起到威慑作用。 这已是12个月内第二起重大蚂蚁走私案。去年，野生动物服务部门拦住了四名自称“蚂蚁帮”的男子。其中有两名 19 岁的比利时人，他们试图将 5,500 名王后走私到欧洲。他们每人被罚款约 5,000 欧元。 每当出现此类情况时，当局通常会叫昆虫学家迪诺·马丁斯到机场。 “我很震惊，”他说。 “不仅因为蚂蚁的数量庞大，还因为它们是蚁后。” 马丁斯表示，被查获的昆虫是从地下巢穴中挖出来的年轻蚁后。马丁斯曾领导过肯尼亚多家研究机构，被认为是非洲领先的蚂蚁专家之一。这些蚁后拥有翅膀，可以让它们飞走并建立新的蚁群。 他说：“当你在这个关键时刻收集蚁后时，你就中断了新蚁群创建的关键阶段。”他补充说，肯尼亚的生态系统也会受到影响，因为蚂蚁会运输草籽，帮助大草原的再生。 在欧洲，饲养蚂蚁作为宠物越来越受欢迎，尤其是在年轻人中。蜂群被安置在玻璃容器中，蜂王在那里产下后代并建立一个全新的种群。 迈克尔·梅尔 (Michael Meier) 是一位以养蚂蚁为爱好的人，他要求不透露自己的真实姓名。在大学期间，他想要一只不需要太多照顾的宠物。 “对于蚂蚁来说，我今天或明天喂它们并不重要，”他说。 迈尔曾一度在一个……中饲养了近 30 个菌落。

title.en: Moscow restaurant blast a 'brutal terror attack,' mayor says
title.zh: 莫斯科市长称餐厅爆炸为“残酷恐怖袭击”

summary.en: An explosion outside an upscale Moscow restaurant at Kudrinskaya Square, described by Mayor Sergei Sobyanin as a "brutal terror attack," resulted in fatalities. The mayor vowed that those responsible would be punished, though many questions about the incident remain unanswered.
summary.zh: 莫斯科市长谢尔盖·索比亚宁称，库德林斯卡亚广场一家高档餐厅外发生的致命爆炸是“残酷的恐怖袭击”，并承诺将惩罚肇事者。然而，关于此事件的许多问题仍未解决。

body.en:
The deadly explosion outside an upscale Moscow restaurant at Kudrinskaya Square was a "brutal terror attack," Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said, promising the perpetrators would be punished. But many questions remain.

An explosion at a restaurant in central Moscow killed at least three people, including the suspected bomber on Saturday night, authorities said.

"Law enforcement agencies are investigating the circumstances of the incident. Those responsible for this crime will certainly be found and face the punishment they deserve," he said in an online post on Sunday.

Russia's Anti-Terrorism Committee said a woman carrying  "a homemade explosive device" tried to enter the restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square but was stopped by a security guard.

The device exploded at the entrance, killing the woman, the guard and a restaurant patron.

State news agency RIA Novosti reported that at least 21 other people were injured in the blast, which occurred shortly before 8 p.m. local time (5 p.m. UTC).

The restaurant's website said the venue had been closed on Saturday for a private event.

Heavily armed law enforcement officers sealed off the area and launched an investigation.

Authorities did not immediately identify those they believed to be behind the attack.

Russia has faced several attacks since the start of the war in Ukraine in 2022. They blamed a ‌series of assassinations and attempted killings on Kyiv. Russian officials have yet to comment on any possible Ukrainian involvement into the Kudrinskaya Square blast.

However, Ukraine used drones to attack other parts of Russia on Saturday evening and early on Sunday, including a bombing which targeted an apartment block and killed two in the city Engels, some 900 kilometers (560 miles) southeast of Moscow.

Russia's Defense Ministry also said Kyiv struck a warehouse belonging to Wildberries, a major online retailer in Russia, with the Ukrainian drones hitting a site in the Samara Oblast, deep inside Russian territory. Regional Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev said it was not immediately clear if there were any casualties.

Russian officials also reported over a 100 Ukrainian strikes in the Belgorod Oblast, which borders Ukraine. They said Kyiv forces used artillery, rocket launchers, and drones, leaving 14 people injured.

Over 200 Ukrainian drones have allegedly been shot down during the wave of attacks.

Meanwhile, at least one person was killed and seven wounded in the Russian attack on Ukraine's Kherson, with the attack involving artillery fire.

In Dnipro, seven passengers were wounded in a drone strike on a minibus, with the regional military administrator Oleksandr Hanzha describing it as a "deliberate and cynical attack on civilians."

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. Produced collectively, many carried no individual author's name, helping transform protest into a shared public voice.

The posters and their messages could appear in dozens of places overnight, giving the protest a wide local visual presence.

Protests also became more impactful when images could be transmitted across borders.

body.zh: 从中华帝国到当今的印度，学生运动不断地采用他们那个时代的工具和符号来挑战权威。 2026 年 7 月 22 日，在多雨的印度孟买，一名穿着休闲的年轻女子走到一辆载着被拘留学生的缓慢行驶的警车前。她将手掌放在引擎盖上，迫使车辆停了下来。 手机从各个角度捕捉了这一时刻。她也举起了自己的手机，记录了这次遭遇。几个小时内，这段视频就传遍了印度及其他地区。 它成为蟑螂简塔党抗议活动的标志性视觉效果之一，在印度医学入学考试泄密后，学生们在这场运动中要求透明度和问责制。 但这一刻的​​力量不仅在于她所做的事情，还在于她的所作所为很快被人们看到。一个年轻女子对抗权威的一个动作，成为了数百万屏幕上共享的符号。 虽然这段视频属于在社交媒体上长大的一代人，但其背后的冲动却要古老得多。 从法庭请愿书和革命海报到照片、雨伞和模因，学生运动不断地调整他们可用的工具和符号，将它们变成异议的工具。 早在电视或社交媒体跨境传播异议之前，学生们就已经找到了表达不满的方法。 例如，在中国东汉，太学的学者与具有改革思想的官员结盟，反对宫廷中有权有势的宦官，许多人认为宦官腐败且在政治上专横。 他们通过公开批评、政治网络和请愿来表达他们的反对意见。 在政治沟通通过官方渠道进行的时代，请愿是向王室表达不满的既定方式之一。它们以正式语言编写并通过官僚机构传达，将学生的担忧直接传达到国家的沟通系统中。 1968 年的巴黎，学生们挑战大学当局和保守的战后社会秩序。随着示威活动在法国首都蔓延并吸引了工人，该运动最持久的贡献之一来自巴黎美术学院的一个地下室工作室。 Atelier Populaire（“人民工作室”）在抗议期间印制了数千张海报，其中许多是在一夜之间印制的。他们大胆的图形、轮廓和口号成为了这场运动的视觉语言。许多作品都是集体制作的，没有作者的名字，这有助于将抗议转变为公众的共同声音。 这些海报及其信息可能会在一夜之间出现在数十个地方，使抗议活动在当地得到广泛的关注。 当图像可以跨境传输时，抗议的影响力也变得更大。 在...

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

Graylin 认为 Kimi K3 的到来将高端人工智能从昂贵的奢侈品变成了实用且负担得起的东西。 “对于 98% 的客户来说，[知识] 1% 到 2% 的差异并不值得多付 10 到 20 倍的费用。” 中国的最新进展已经引起华盛顿的强烈反应，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普现在威胁要阻止美国使用中国的人工智能模型。 与此同时，财政部长斯科特·贝森特本周早些时候警告称，美国可能会因涉嫌盗窃知识产权而制裁中国模型。 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 指责中国实验室使用他们的模型来训练他们自己的系统，这一过程被称为蒸馏。 虽然提炼是全球人工智能实验室在一定程度上的常见做法，但这些公司表示，他们的模型已经受到查询的轰炸，以收获高级推理。白宫四月份警告说，中国正在以“工业规模”这样做。 北京方面予以反击，否认这些指控毫无根据，并称美国威胁实施制裁和示范禁令是“技术欺凌”，旨在遏制中国的崛起。 华盛顿智库史汀生中心战略远见中心的研究分析师朱莉娅·尼赫（Giulia Neaher）淡化了提炼在基米进步中的作用。 “[其成功]很大程度上归功于为建设这个项目而投入的人才、基础设施和资源......

title.en: 'Steadfast advocate': Arnhem Land's Rirratjingu clan elder Bakamumu Marika dies
title.zh: “坚定的倡导者”：阿纳姆地Rirratjingu部落长老巴卡穆穆·马里卡去世

summary.en: Bakamumu Marika, a Rirratjingu clan elder from Arnhem Land, has passed away. He was known for his lifelong dedication to fighting for land rights and championing Indigenous people.
summary.zh: 阿纳姆地Rirratjingu部落长老巴卡穆穆·马里卡去世。他一生致力于为土地权利和原住民争取权益。

body.en:
A respected elder of Arnhem Land's Rirratjingu clan, Bakamumu Marika AM, has died, the clan group's Aboriginal corporation has announced.

"It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of Bakamumu Marika AM, a highly respected Traditional Owner, elder and senior leader of the Rirratjingu Clan," the statement said.

Marika was a founder, long-serving chairman and current patron of the Rirratjingu Aboriginal Corporation who was appointed a Member of the Order of Australia (AM) in 2022 for his significant community service to North-East Arnhem Land.

As a "steadfast advocate" for land rights, Marika continued one of the most significant legacies in Australia’s Indigenous rights history, honouring and advancing the work of his forefathers, the statement reads.

body.en:
Two people have been hospitalised after a building collapsed in central Sydney on Monday, emergency services said.

A spokesperson for New South Wales Ambulance said it was called to an address in Ultimo, a suburb around 2 km from the city's central business district, just before 11am.

Workers assessed seven patients at the scene. According to ABC News, one man in his 60s and another in his 30s were removed from the rubble and rushed to hospital in a serious condition.

One of the men was taken to St Vincent's Hospital Sydney. The other was taken to Royal Prince Alfred Hospital.

Fire and Rescue New South Wales (FRNSW) told ABC News that the building was a construction site. Nearby buildings, including an adjoining service station, have been evacuated.

title.en: 'Deeply saddened': Australian helicopter provider speaks after Greece firefighting tragedy
title.zh: “深感悲痛”：希腊消防悲剧后，澳大利亚直升机供应商发声

summary.en: McDermott Aviation, an Australian helicopter provider, has expressed profound sadness following a firefighting tragedy in Greece, where helicopters leased by the company were involved as wildfires continue to spread across southern Europe.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚直升机供应商麦克德莫特航空对希腊消防悲剧表示深切哀悼，该公司租赁的直升机参与了扑灭南欧持续蔓延的野火。

body.en:
Two crew members have died after two helicopters — leased by Australian company McDermott Aviation — collided midair while battling wildfires in Greece on Sunday.

A Greek and a Danish national were killed in the crash over Psatha, an area west of Athens, according to Greece's fire service. Two crew members from Greece and Britain who were operating a separate helicopter were found alive.

Founder and president of McDermott Aviation, John McDermott said he was "deeply saddened" by news of the fatal collision.

"We are deeply saddened to confirm that the two crew members aboard one of the helicopters have lost their lives. The two crew members from the second helicopter are in the care of medical professionals.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with the families, friends and colleagues of those affected by this tragic incident. Both crews were undertaking the critical work of supporting firefighting operations to help protect communities."

McDermott Aviation has reportedly operated in Greece for several years. The company said it is working closely with relevant authorities as they undertake an investigation into the cause of the incident.

Over the past decade, McDermott Aviation said it has engaged in around 10 to 12 international movements a year via sea and air freight. It also operates in New Caledonia, Papua New Guinea, Indonesia and the United States, which is currently experiencing wildfires in several western states.

Nikos Pagiotelis has been a volunteer firefighter in Greece for more than 20 years. He told SBS Greek about the moment he heard news of the crash over local radio.

"When you are inside the fire, and you are trying to help the people, you're trying to save the animals, save the forest. Then suddenly [you] hear that two helicopters have crashed a couple of miles near you — you can understand that something really hurts inside," Pagiotelis said.

"You can do nothing, you freeze for a little bit, and then you just continue your work. You continue to help people to honour the lives of the loss of two comrades."

In a statement on social media, Greek prime minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis also expressed his "sorrow for the tragic accident" and extended condolences to the families of the deceased firefighters.

"The loss of the Greek coordinator and the Danish pilot at the time they were attempting the major fire in Porto Gremeno fills us all with grief," Mitsotakis said.

Nearly 500 firefighters and 23 aircraft have been deployed to fight fires in Greece, which have been driven by high temperatures and gale-force winds.

title.en: Big tech companies could be hit with higher taxes if they don't strike deals with publishers
title.zh: 如果大型科技公司不与出版商达成协议，它们可能会面临更高的税收

summary.en: Tech giants criticised the previous draft laws released in April. What's changed?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Tech firms will pay a higher levy or strike more deals to avoid the charge under planned tweaks to an initiative to force them to hand over some of their revenue to media companies.

The proposed news bargaining incentive will push companies like Google, Meta and TikTok to strike commercial deals with news organisations to use the publishers' content on their platforms.

If deals are struck, the companies will pay a smaller share of their Australian advertising revenues to the government than if they refuse to reach agreements.

The levy will apply to tech giants with domestic revenues of $250 million or more, with any funds raised to be redistributed to the media sector.

But after a consultation period on the changes, which Labor hopes to legislate when parliament returns in Spring, elements of the incentive have been tipped further in favour of news publishers.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The maximum levy that tech companies will pay on their revenue has been increased from 2.5 per cent from a previously proposed 2.25 per cent charge, the government revealed on Monday.

They will also have to strike at least six deals with publishers — rather than four — to fully discharge the liability.

But the revenue used to calculate the tech giants' payments will be limited to digital advertising income attributable to the Australian market.

Assistant Treasurer Daniel Mulino said the government had shown good faith in negotiating with both the platforms and media companies during the consultation process.

"Australian journalism is important to a well-functioning democracy and we want it to be sustainable now and into the future," he said.

"We want digital platforms to do deals with a diverse range of media organisations."

Approved agreements with large media companies would allow tech companies to offset 150 per cent of their liabilities, while deals with smaller firms attract a 200 per cent offset — up from 170 per cent under previous plans.

A professional networking platform carve-out that would have excluded LinkedIn has been scrapped.

The previous draft laws, released in April, were heavily criticised by the tech giants as "a government-mandated transfer of wealth from one industry to another".

body.zh: 科技公司将支付更高的税款或达成更多交易，以避免根据计划调整的一项举措，迫使它们将部分收入交给媒体公司的收费。 拟议的新闻讨价还价激励措施将推动谷歌、Meta 和 TikTok 等公司与新闻机构达成商业协议，在其平台上使用出版商​​的内容。 如果达成协议，这些公司将比拒绝达成协议的情况下向政府支付更少的澳大利亚广告收入份额。 该税将适用于国内收入达到或超过 2.5 亿美元的科技巨头，筹集的任何资金将重新分配给媒体行业。 但工党希望在议会春季复会时对这些改革进行立法，经过一段咨询期后，激励措施的要素进一步向有利于新闻出版商的方向倾斜。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 政府周一透露，科技公司对其收入缴纳的最高税率已从之前提议的 2.25% 提高到 2.5%。 他们还必须与出版商达成至少六项协议（而不是四项）才能完全履行责任。 但用于计算科技巨头付款的收入将仅限于归属于澳大利亚市场的数字广告收入。 助理财长丹尼尔·穆利诺表示，政府在咨询过程中与平台和媒体公司的谈判都表现出了诚意。 “澳大利亚新闻业对于一个运转良好的民主国家非常重要，我们希望它在现在和未来都能够可持续发展，”他说。 “我们希望数字平台能够与各种媒体组织达成交易。” 与大型媒体公司达成的批准协议将允许科技公司抵消 150% 的负债，而与小公司的交易则可获得 200% 的抵消——高于之前计划的 170%。 原本将 LinkedIn 排除在外的专业网络平台分拆已被取消。 此前于四月份发布的法律草案遭到科技巨头的严厉批评，称其为“政府强制将财富从一个行业转移到另一个行业”。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

title.en: Home prices fall across Australia as housing downturn takes hold
title.zh: 澳大利亚房价下跌，楼市低迷

summary.en: National home prices recorded their biggest monthly decline since 2022, with Sydney and Melbourne leading the falls.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚全国房价录得自2022年以来的最大月度跌幅，其中悉尼和墨尔本领跌。

body.en:
Australia's housing market downturn is spreading across the country as higher interest rates and changes to property taxes take hold.

Figures from property analytics company Cotality showed national home prices fell 0.7 per cent last month, the largest single-month decline since December 2022.

Annual growth has slowed to 5.3 per cent, well below the double-digit pace recorded earlier this year.

The country's largest property markets, Sydney and Melbourne, recorded declines of 1.4 per cent and 1.2 per cent respectively. Both cities are more than five per cent lower than recent peaks.

Brisbane and Adelaide, where prices have recently boomed, also recorded drops of 0.6 and 0.2 per cent respectively.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

In Perth, which has recorded the strongest year-on-year growth of any capital city at 21.8 per cent , prices were virtually flat, rising just 0.1 per cent.

"For buyers who remain in the market, lower competition and elevated stock levels (when compared with the start of the year) mean greater choice and more negotiating power," the property analytics firm said.

However, the fall in prices has been led by properties at the higher end of the market, providing little benefit to first home-buyers who are also grappling with lower borrowing capacity after three interest rate hikes this year.

Homes in the top quarter of the market lost 3.2 per cent of their value in the three months to July, compared to a 0.3 per cent gain in the lower-price tier.

Beyond the capital cities, the regional property market recorded a drop a 0.2 per cent — the first decline since January 2023.

"There remains a mismatch between the pricing expectations of buyers and sellers," Cotality head of research Gerard Burg said.

Consumer sentiment has also been soured by high living costs, uncertainty caused by the ongoing Middle East war and tax changes announced in the May budget.

"We have observed a deterioration in the flow of new listings across the country in recent weeks, led by Sydney, as potential vendors assess a weak market and choose to wait until conditions improve," Burg said.

Rental prices have continued to rise due to low vacancy rates. Burg said national median rents had risen by more than $200 a week in the last five years.

"Despite the tight market conditions, there are question marks about how much further rents can rise," he said.

body.en:
Strata and building managers are being contacted by the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) ahead of the 2026 Census to help facilitate access to secure apartment buildings.

As president of the Strata Community Association of Australasia, Joshua Baldwin has been informing building managers about  the Census process .

He said while Census data collected by the ABS provides important insights into the nation's population and housing, coordinating access to secure-building apartments can become a "logistical nightmare".

Around 30,000 field staff have been hired by the ABS to ensure everyone in Australia is counted on 11 August. This involves delivering Census materials before Census night and following up with households that have not completed their Census after 11 August.

"We get a lot of questions as to why ... they need access onto our property and who is going to be [there]," Baldwin told SBS News.

SBS News has seen correspondence between ABS staff and a Melbourne-based strata management firm.

The email outlines access arrangements for secure apartment buildings during Census activities, including requests for entry to prescribed premises between 8am and 8pm on weekdays and from 9am to 8pm on weekends. The ABS expects Census-related visits will conclude by the end of September.

In circumstances where Census staff cannot meet with onsite management to access buildings, the ABS may request temporary access arrangements, including apartment keys, fob cards or passcodes for secure areas.

Baldwin said he had heard of instances where "some Census officers have ... just straight up demanded access" to keys.

"Unfortunately, you know, we can't provide that access without the permission of the strata corporation," he said.

He acknowledged these interactions were rare and said, in most cases, facilitating building access was "quite fluid and quite easy".

To avoid handing over keys directly, Baldwin said some strata managers have established temporary box systems outside buildings, allowing authorised access while maintaining security arrangements.

For more than a century, the ABS has conducted the Census to provide a snapshot of Australia . The data collected helps inform understanding of the nation's population, housing and communities.

This includes information about Australian residents, international visitors and people on temporary visas.

It was once a dream of many: work hard and retire in your 60s. Now, more Australians are employed into their 70s, 80s and even 90s. Insight meets those still working by choice, those who can't afford to stop, and asks what happens when you keep working later in life? Watch Insight episode Working Later in Life Tuesday 8.30pm on SBS or SBS On Demand.

Keiri Easdown retired as a professional dancer at the age of 45 when the work became too physically demanding. She never imagined that nearly three decades on, she would have tried four more careers and still be working.

"It was a rude shock really — having to do something like give up dancing," she tells Insight. "That was who I was; it was my life."

Leaving a physically demanding career — and one that also didn't allow her to save much money — the single mum had to retrain to earn a living and support her two children.

"Whatever I earned pretty much went out of the house; it paid the rent, it paid the bills for my children."

Since leaving behind her dance career, the 73-year-old has pivoted careers upwards of four times.

She's been an entertainment director at Gold Coast theme park Dreamworld, did some time in retail and corporate for a whitegoods company, and worked as a cleaner, before that became too physically taxing in her mid-60s.

On average, Australians plan to retire between their 65th and 66th birthdays, according to data released in 2024 by the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS).

But Keiri, who has been working as a teacher aide at the school her daughter and son-in-law teach at since her late 60s, says she needs to keep working.

"I have very little in superannuation. As a dancer, we didn't earn much. We lived hand to mouth."

The average age of the 156,000 people who retired in the 2024-2025 financial year was 63.8, according to the ABS. Their exit from the workforce brought the nation's total number of retirees (aged 45 years and over) to 4.5 million.

The 2025 Household, Income and Labour Dynamics in Australia (HILDA) survey conducted by the University of Melbourne's Melbourne Institute found that, even though women are still retiring slightly earlier than men (a year on average), they are staying in the workforce longer than they once did.

In 2003, 69.5 per cent of women and 48.5 per cent of men in the 60-64 age group were retired. Twenty years later, these figures had dropped to 40.8 per cent and 27.4 per cent, respectively.

title.en: 'That was crazy': Australia's historic Commonwealth Games day ends with a bizarre twist

summary.en: A midnight medal ceremony and a scaled-back format made for an unconventional Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

body.en:
The Australian athletics team had its biggest one-day medal haul at the Commonwealth Games on Saturday, ending with a peculiar medal ceremony in a near-empty stadium.

Hours after the Games' athletics program ended, the Aussie men's sprinters were still waiting for their victory to be confirmed after protests over the other podium placings.

When the 4x100 relay team collected their medals in a makeshift ceremony along with the Canadian silver and Nigerian bronze medallists, the clock was ticking towards midnight.

The crowds at Glasgow's Scotstoun Stadium were long gone, with less than a hundred people remaining — mostly made up of Games officials, team staff, journalists and volunteers.

It was an odd ceremony for a major championship, with Australian winner Josh Azzopardi admitting with a smile: "That was crazy! We'd been waiting around not really knowing what was going to happen. It's definitely unique."

"We won gold, felt like it was ages ago now," said his teammate Lachlan Kennedy.

The holdup was the result of Canada's protests over their initial disqualification for a supposed illegal changeover, which was first upheld and then deliberated upon by the jury at great length until Canada was cleared for the silver.

It was an unusual conclusion to Australia's most successful athletics day ever at the Games, with a record haul of seven gold medals and 17 medals in total, including two events where the Aussies swept the podium.

Australia's previous record was set more than 70 years ago, with six gold medals and 11 medals in total in 1950.

It capped off the penultimate day of a stripped-back Games that had been quirky from the outset .

Victoria was originally supposed to host , but withdrew in 2023 due to rising costs. At the time, it prompted some to question the relevance of the Games and whether the event had a future at all.

The following year, organisers announced that Glasgow would step in as host city, with its Games to be supported in part by money from Victoria. The Victorian government had to pay a compensation of $589m including a $380 million settlement to cancel its hosting obligations.

While the Games has always had fewer sports and athletes than the Olympics, the 2026 event was even more pared back.

The 2022 Birmingham Games featured 20 sports and more than 5,000 athletes, while Glasgow hosted just 3,000 athletes competing in ten sports.

Some onlookers said the vibes in the city were vastly different to 2014, when it last hosted the Games.
